newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl calls for end to row in German coalition.
newsitem.headline: Kohl calls for end to row in German coalition.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl called for an end to the squabbling in his fractious centre-right coalition government on Monday and threw his full support behind embattled Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
Kohl, who returned from a week-long trip to the Far East on Saturday, said his Christian Democratic Party (CDU) wanted to keep the coalition together.

But he warned the Free Democrats (FDP), junior partners in the coalition, that they would be making a mistake if they thought they could raise their own political profile at the expense of the CDU and its Bavarian sister party, the CSU.
"We want this coalition and we want it to continue," Kohl said after a meeting of CDU leaders.

"Anyone in any of the coalition parties who believes they can raise their profile at the cost of the others is mistaken," Kohl added. "The coalition is successful as a whole and everyone has their share in it."

The FDP has made repeated attacks in recent weeks on Waigel, whom it blames for serious problems in the 1997 budget. The party was forced to swallow a painful defeat last month when its pledge to cut the so-called "Solidarity" income tax surcharge in 1997 was scrapped.
"Theo Waigel deserves all out support, especially in this difficult time," Kohl said. "I say that quite clearly as chancellor and chairman of the CDU."
